findings.title: _detect_cycles uses unbounded recursive DFS + _set_story_deps wipes all deps on cycle
findings.description: _detect_cycles (line 265) uses a recursive inner function `dfs()` with no depth limit. Python default recursion limit is 1000. A dependency graph with 300+ stories in a chain will raise RecursionError, crashing the MCP tool. Additionally, _set_story_deps (line 297) deletes ALL dependencies of a story when any cycle is detected (line 323: `DELETE FROM story_dependencies WHERE story_id = ?`), wiping legitimate deps if a single new dep is cyclic.
findings.current_code_summary: Recursive dfs() function at line 276 with path.append/pop and in_stack tracking. _set_story_deps at line 316 calls _detect_cycles, and on any cycle involving story_id, runs DELETE FROM story_dependencies WHERE story_id = ? — removing all deps, not just the cyclic one.
findings.fix_approach: Convert _detect_cycles to iterative DFS using explicit stack. In _set_story_deps, only remove the newly-added deps that created cycles: track which dep_ids were just inserted, and on cycle detection, only remove those specific deps that are part of the cycle path, keeping pre-existing deps intact.
findings.what_could_break: If iterative DFS has different cycle detection semantics (e.g., misses multi-node cycles), existing valid dep graphs could incorrectly detect cycles. Test with: no deps, linear chain, diamond, actual cycle, near-cycle.

findings.title: pm_triage WHERE clause contradiction returns empty backlog when epic_id given
findings.description: The backlog query hardcodes `WHERE s.epic_id = 'epic-backlog'` then conditionally appends `AND s.epic_id = ?` with the user's epic_id. This creates `epic_id = 'epic-backlog' AND epic_id = '<user_epic>'` — impossible condition, always returns 0 rows for backlog section when epic_id is provided.
findings.current_code_summary: Line 133-136: f-string SQL with hardcoded epic-backlog condition + conditional AND epic_id = ? appended when epic_id parameter is set.
findings.fix_approach: Skip the backlog query entirely when epic_id is given. Only query backlog stories when doing the full triage view (epic_id is None). The other triage sections (unassigned, draft_without_tasks) already use epic_filter correctly.
findings.what_could_break: None — this purely fixes a bug. The backlog section was always empty with epic_id anyway.

findings.title: pm_create_story hardcodes task IDs t1/t2 causing potential collision
findings.description: pm_create_story inserts tasks with hardcoded `task_id = f't{i}'` starting at t1 (line 164). The helper _add_task_to_story correctly computes next ID via MAX query. If tasks are deleted and re-created, the hardcoded path can collide. Same issue in pm_plan_items (lines 338-344).
findings.current_code_summary: Lines 163-169: `for i, task_title in enumerate(tasks or [], start=1): task_id = f't{i}'` with direct INSERT. _add_task_to_story (line 433 in helpers) already exists and computes MAX+1.
findings.fix_approach: Replace the inline loop with calls to _add_task_to_story(conn, story_id, task_title). Already imported in tools_pm_write.py (line 27). Fix same pattern in pm_plan_items (line 338-344).
findings.what_could_break: Minimal — _add_task_to_story produces the same IDs on a fresh story, just with one extra SELECT per task.

findings.title: Duplicated embedding utilities between tools_knowledge.py and hooks/lib/embedding_utils.py
findings.description: tools_knowledge.py defines _get_embedding() (timeout=30s) and _embedding_to_blob() as local functions identical to hooks/lib/embedding_utils.py (timeout=10s). MCP server runs from mcp-servers/gemini/ and can't directly import hooks.lib without sys.path manipulation.
findings.fix_approach: In tools_knowledge.py, add PROJECT_ROOT parent to sys.path and import get_embedding and embedding_to_blob from hooks.lib.embedding_utils. Use 30s timeout as parameter or accept the 10s default (Ollama should already be loaded). Delete the local _get_embedding and _embedding_to_blob functions.
findings.what_could_break: If import path is wrong, _om_shadow_decision fails silently (catches all exceptions). Timeout change from 30s to 10s — 10s is fine since Ollama should be loaded.

findings.title: Three near-identical _ensure_*_column functions
findings.description: _ensure_order_idx_column (329), _ensure_read_files_column (341), _ensure_test_files_column (353) follow identical try/ALTER TABLE/catch-duplicate pattern. Only difference is column name, type, and optional default.
findings.fix_approach: Consolidate into _ensure_column(conn, table, name, col_type, default=None). Replace three functions with calls to _ensure_column in startup_migrate. The _ensure_epic_columns function (line 365) already uses a loop — extend its pattern.
findings.what_could_break: None — pure refactor of startup-only code.

findings.title: Stale CHECK constraint in _ensure_knowledge_tables patterns CREATE TABLE
findings.description: _ensure_knowledge_tables creates patterns table with CHECK (category IN ('react', 'firebase', ...)). Migration v5 (line 135-158) drops this constraint. The CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS won't re-fire if table exists, but the initial schema should match the v5 target (no category CHECK).
findings.fix_approach: Remove the CHECK (category IN (...)) from line 410 in the CREATE TABLE statement. Keep severity and status CHECK constraints as they are still valid.
findings.what_could_break: None — removing CHECK makes schema more permissive.

findings.title: globals().update obscures MCP tools from static analysis
findings.description: 12 calls to globals().update(_r_*(mcp) or {}) inject tool function names into module namespace. FastMCP registers tools at @mcp.tool() decoration time — the globals().update is unnecessary for tool registration.
findings.fix_approach: Remove all globals().update(...) calls. Replace with plain calls: `_r_gemini(mcp)`, `_r_test(mcp)`, etc. No code imports tool functions from server.py by name.

downstream_tools: All MCP tools — but registration is via @mcp.tool() decorator

findings.what_could_break: If any code imports tools by name from server.py — grep confirms none do. The __main__ block references only startup_migrate, _get_db, _migrate_pitfalls.

findings.title: Silent embedding failures return null — no logging, no way to diagnose
findings.description: get_embedding() returns None on any error (URLError, OSError, JSONDecodeError, KeyError) with no logging. Callers (om_write.py, signal_processor.py, stop_processor.py, tools_knowledge.py, update-prompts-index.py) treat None as 'unavailable' and silently degrade. No way to know embedding system is broken. om_write.py already logs 'ollama_fallback' at line 65 but only after dedup_check — the initial failure is silent.
findings.fix_approach: Add sys.stderr logging in get_embedding() on failure, similar to om_write.py's existing pattern. Keep None return for backward compatibility. Log the exception type and message so failures are visible in hook stderr output.
findings.what_could_break: Adding logging changes no behavior. Stderr output goes to hook logs, not user terminal.

findings.title: Cost calc defaults to Opus pricing for non-matching models
findings.description: compute_cost() only checks `if 'opus' in model`, everything else gets Sonnet pricing ($3/$15). Haiku ($0.25/$1.25) gets charged at Sonnet rates — 12x overestimate. Any future models also default to Sonnet.
findings.current_code_summary: 7-line function: if 'opus' in model -> Opus rates, else -> Sonnet rates. No haiku branch, no unknown model handling.
findings.fix_approach: Add explicit 'haiku' check with correct pricing ($0.25 input, $0.3125 cache_creation, $0.025 cache_read, $1.25 output per 1M). Add 'sonnet' check. Default unknown models to Sonnet pricing with stderr warning.
findings.what_could_break: Historical cost data computed with wrong rates won't retroactively change. New sessions use correct rates.

findings.title: Unvalidated JSON input in hooks — repeated inline parsing pattern
findings.description: 10+ hooks parse JSON from stdin via `echo "$INPUT" | python3 -c 'import sys, json; d = json.load(sys.stdin); ...'` with `2>/dev/null`. If INPUT is empty/malformed, extracted value is empty string, hook falls through to default behavior. Impossible to debug. Same pattern copy-pasted 10+ times.
findings.fix_approach: Create hooks/lib/parse_hook_input.py — a standalone Python script: reads stdin JSON, extracts dot-path field (e.g., 'tool_input.file_path'), prints it, exits 0 on any error with empty output. Usage: `VALUE=$(echo "$INPUT" | python3 "$CLAUDE_ROOT/hooks/lib/parse_hook_input.py" tool_input.file_path)`. Migrate 2-3 hooks as proof of concept; full migration in follow-up.
findings.what_could_break: New helper with different semantics could break hooks. Start with helper + migrate 2 hooks; full migration is follow-up.
